t: Section 807 of the Housing and Community Development Amendments of 1978 is amended by striking out “$10,000,000” and inserting in lieu thereof “$5,000,000”.

fable.w: This section only changes a dollar figure in an existing statute. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue for any party outside the federal government. There is no tempting reading here, since nothing in the text describes a process bringing outsiders into a federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking out “$10,000,000” and inserting in lieu thereof “$5,000,000”.

opus.w: This section only changes a dollar figure in Section 807 of the Housing and Community Development Amendments of 1978, from $10,000,000 to $5,000,000. It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, rulemaking authority or right to sue. Reading in participation because of the housing program context is wrong, since the text itself brings no one from outside the federal government into a decision.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The Housing and Community Development Amendments of 1978 cover programs that may involve local governments or the public. That might seem to suggest participation. It doesn't hold up, because this section only changes a dollar amount. It involves no outside party in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple legislative amendment that changes a specific dollar amount in a previous statute. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, advisory committees, consultation with states or tribes, or any other form of participation by non-federal entities. The action is purely internal to the legislative process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 807 of the Housing and Community Development Amendments of 1978 is amended by striking out “$10,000,000” and inserting in lieu thereof “$5,000,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing funding levels affects how programs are run and thus involves public input, but the text itself is purely a legislative amendment to a dollar figure. It does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, or coordination with outside parties.
